timeprovider-deterministic-time-tests.title: Test time-dependent code deterministically with TimeProvider
timeprovider-deterministic-time-tests.short: Inject clock and timer behavior instead of waiting for wall-clock time
timeprovider-deterministic-time-tests.summary: Accepting TimeProvider as a dependency separates code that uses current time, elapsed time, or timers from the machine's real clock.
timeprovider-deterministic-time-tests.why: Embedding DateTime.UtcNow or real delays directly makes tests slower and makes boundary times or long elapsed periods difficult to reproduce.
timeprovider-deterministic-time-tests.tips: Centralize time access through TimeProvider, use System in production, and inject a controllable provider in tests.

pipereader-read-advance-contract.title: Understand the PipeReader Read and AdvanceTo contract
pipereader-read-advance-contract.short: Report consumed and examined positions correctly for each read buffer
pipereader-read-advance-contract.summary: PipeReader returns a buffer from ReadAsync and expects the consumer to report how far it consumed and examined that buffer with AdvanceTo.
pipereader-read-advance-contract.why: Incorrect positions can discard unprocessed bytes or retain already-inspected data and increase memory usage.
pipereader-read-advance-contract.tips: Do not retain a ReadResult buffer across the next read, distinguish consumed from examined, and make sure every read path eventually advances the reader.

concurrentdictionary-valuefactory-reexec.title: ConcurrentDictionary value factories may run more than once
concurrentdictionary-valuefactory-reexec.short: Do not treat a GetOrAdd factory as exactly-once execution
concurrentdictionary-valuefactory-reexec.summary: ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd publishes one winning value, but under contention its value factory can execute concurrently more than once.
concurrentdictionary-valuefactory-reexec.why: External side effects or expensive initialization directly inside the factory can therefore be duplicated.
concurrentdictionary-valuefactory-reexec.tips: Keep factories free of side effects or store a Lazy<T> so initialization of the underlying value has its own exactly-once coordination.

filesystemwatcher-events-not-transaction.title: Do not treat FileSystemWatcher events as committed file transactions
filesystemwatcher-events-not-transaction.short: Design for duplicate, bursty, and occasionally lost notifications
filesystemwatcher-events-not-transaction.summary: FileSystemWatcher exposes operating-system change notifications, not a transactional one-event-per-logical-operation protocol.
filesystemwatcher-events-not-transaction.why: One save can produce several events, internal buffers can overflow, and a notification can arrive while a writer is still modifying the file.
filesystemwatcher-events-not-transaction.tips: Use events as triggers, debounce or rescan as needed, and treat the final filesystem state as authoritative.

immutablearray-default-vs-empty.title: Distinguish default ImmutableArray<T> from Empty
immutablearray-default-vs-empty.short: An uninitialized value and an initialized zero-length array are different states
immutablearray-default-vs-empty.summary: ImmutableArray<T> is a value type and has a default state that is distinct from the explicit empty array represented by ImmutableArray<T>.Empty.
immutablearray-default-vs-empty.why: Mixing the states at API boundaries can obscure whether a caller meant not-specified or an explicitly empty collection.
immutablearray-default-vs-empty.tips: Decide whether the uninitialized state belongs in the contract, normalize to Empty when it does not, and document default when it intentionally represents a third state.

ratelimit-lease-metadata-disposal.title: Handle RateLimitLease outcome, metadata, and lifetime together
ratelimit-lease-metadata-disposal.short: Use RetryAfter and other metadata instead of checking only acquisition
ratelimit-lease-metadata-disposal.summary: System.Threading.RateLimiting returns a RateLimitLease that carries the acquisition result and optional metadata supplied by the limiter.
ratelimit-lease-metadata-disposal.why: Checking only IsAcquired can discard useful retry information and leave lease lifetime unclear.
ratelimit-lease-metadata-disposal.tips: Dispose leases explicitly, inspect supported metadata, and feed that information into response or retry policy where appropriate.

httpclient-cookiecontainer-handler-shari.title: Define cookie-state boundaries when sharing HttpClient handlers
httpclient-cookiecontainer-handler-shari.short: Connection reuse and cookie sharing are separate design decisions
httpclient-cookiecontainer-handler-shari.summary: CookieContainer belongs to the HttpMessageHandler state, so clients backed by a reused handler can share cookie state across otherwise separate call sites.
httpclient-cookiecontainer-handler-shari.why: Putting requests from different users or trust boundaries through the same cookie container can mix state and send cookies unintentionally.
httpclient-cookiecontainer-handler-shari.tips: Isolate cookie state by session or trust boundary, or disable automatic cookies and manage required Cookie headers explicitly.

libraryimport-source-generated-interop.title: Use LibraryImport for source-generated P/Invoke boundaries
libraryimport-source-generated-interop.short: Generate supported marshalling code ahead of runtime
libraryimport-source-generated-interop.summary: LibraryImportAttribute source-generates P/Invoke marshalling code for supported signatures, reducing reliance on runtime-generated interop stubs.
libraryimport-source-generated-interop.why: Native boundaries contain implicit assumptions about strings, ownership, and calling conventions, and those assumptions also affect AOT and performance.
libraryimport-source-generated-interop.tips: Specify marshalling deliberately, follow generator diagnostics, and model ownership of native resources separately with SafeHandle where appropriate.

backgroundservice-cooperative-shutdown.title: Shut down BackgroundService cooperatively with stoppingToken
backgroundservice-cooperative-shutdown.short: Propagate host shutdown into waits and I/O inside the worker
backgroundservice-cooperative-shutdown.summary: The stoppingToken passed to BackgroundService.ExecuteAsync is the main signal for long-running work to respond to host shutdown.
backgroundservice-cooperative-shutdown.why: Checking the token only in the outer loop while inner I/O or waits ignore it can leave the service running long after shutdown was requested.
backgroundservice-cooperative-shutdown.tips: Pass the token through queue waits, I/O, delays, and other cancellable work, then keep final cleanup bounded.

objectdisposedexception-concurrent-lifet.title: ObjectDisposedException from concurrent lifetime races
objectdisposedexception-concurrent-lifet.short: Do not let one operation dispose a shared resource while another still uses it
objectdisposedexception-concurrent-lifet.summary: When asynchronous or concurrent operations share a disposable resource, disposal by one owner can race with use by another and surface as ObjectDisposedException.
objectdisposedexception-concurrent-lifet.why: Null checks or blind retries do not solve the ownership race, and timing-dependent failures are difficult to reproduce.
objectdisposedexception-concurrent-lifet.tips: Assign disposal responsibility to one owner, wait for active users before disposal, and introduce explicit lifetime or reference-counting boundaries when sharing is unavoidable.
